## Comment

*1. Purpose.* Peacemaking depends on candor. Participants speak more openly when they know that what they say will not be used against them later.[^candor] Subsection (a) states a broad rule of confidentiality, and subsection (b) backs it with a privilege that a participant can assert in a later proceeding.

*2. Citation forms.* This paragraph exists to test citations. A uniform act cited by section [@specimen-uniform-mediation-act, § 4]. The same act again, at another section [@specimen-uniform-mediation-act, § 5]. A section of the United States Code with a subsection pinpoint [@usc-25-5130, (2)]. The same section at another subsection [@usc-25-5130, (3)]. A case with a page pinpoint [@specimen-santa-clara-pueblo-v-martinez, 52]. The uniform act once more, now as a short form [@specimen-uniform-mediation-act, § 6].

*3. Choosing between the alternatives.* Alternative A gives the peacemaker a veto over waiver. Alternative B leaves waiver to the participants alone. The table compares them.

| Question | Alternative A | Alternative B |
|---|---|---|
| Who must sign a waiver? | Every participant and the peacemaker | Every participant |
| Can the peacemaker block disclosure? | Yes | No |
| Can the peacemaker be compelled to testify? | Only with the peacemaker's consent | No |

*4. Exceptions.* The exceptions in subsection (c) are narrow. Each reflects a judgment that a competing interest, such as physical safety or the protection of a child, outweighs confidentiality in the circumstance described.[^narrow]

## Illustrations

1. P and Q take part in a peacemaking session about a boundary fence. During the session, P says that P moved the fence posts. No agreement is reached, and Q later sues P. Under subsection (a), Q may not offer P's statement in evidence.

2. Same facts as Illustration 1, except that the parties sign an agreement in which P acknowledges moving the posts. Under subsection (c)(1), the signed agreement is not protected.

3. During a session, R tells the peacemaker that R intends to harm a named neighbor that evening. Under subsection (c)(2)(A), the statement is not confidential.
